items.prompt: Under what exact condition does a mutation fail with the board.version_conflict error?
items.answer: Only when the client sent an X-Board-Version header AND its value differs from the board's current Version - omitting the header skips the check entirely
distractors: Whenever two mutations hit the same board concurrently, regardless of headers
When the request body's version field is older than the stored aggregate's
Whenever the header is missing, since every mutation requires a version token
items.explanation: MutateAsync guards with `expectedVersion is not null && board.Version != expectedVersion.Value`, and ReadExpectedVersion returns null when the header is absent - the critique flags this opt-in design as risk 4.

items.prompt: A client calls move-column with position 999 on a board that has four columns. What happens?
items.answer: The column simply lands at the end: the position is clamped into range and every column is reindexed to a dense 0..n sequence
distractors: A 400 validation.non_negative error, because 999 is outside the column range
The column keeps position 999, leaving a gap in the ordering
A 409 conflict, since moving past the last slot implies a stale client
items.explanation: MoveColumn inserts at Math.Clamp(position, 0, _columns.Count) and then ReindexColumns rewrites every Position to its list index - out-of-range input is normalized, not rejected.

items.prompt: The default 'Backlog' and 'Done' columns are created with cardLimit 0, while 'In progress' gets 4. What does a limit of 0 mean?
items.answer: Unlimited - the invariant only throws when CardLimit is positive and the count exceeds it
distractors: The column is frozen: a 0-limit column rejects every AddCard with a conflict
The limit is unset and inherited from the board's default of 10
Zero is rejected at construction, so those columns actually get limit 1
items.explanation: EnsureCardLimit's guard is `CardLimit > 0 && _cards.Count > CardLimit`, so 0 disables the check; a breach throws DomainException.Conflict with code column.card_limit.

items.prompt: MoveCard removes the card from its source column before adding it to the target, and the target's card-limit check can throw after the removal. Why is the stored board never left missing a card?
items.answer: UpdateAsync runs the mutation on a clone and only swaps it into the dictionary on success - a thrown invariant abandons the half-mutated copy
distractors: A compensating transaction re-inserts the card into the source column in a catch block
The card-limit check runs before any removal, so the sequence can never throw mid-move
The write lock rolls back the dictionary entry when the update delegate throws
items.explanation: The repository does `update(existing.Clone())` and assigns `_boards[boardId]` only after update returns; an exception propagates before the assignment, leaving the last consistent clone in place.

items.prompt: DELETE /api/boards/{id}/cards/{id} routes to ArchiveCardAsync. What does 'archiving' actually do to the card?
items.answer: It removes the card from its column and drops it - nothing stores archived cards, so the operation is an irreversible delete
distractors: It moves the card to a hidden Archive column kept on every board
It flags the card IsArchived so list responses can filter it out
It serializes the card to disk before removal so it can be restored
items.explanation: Board.ArchiveCard is RemoveCard + Touch; the Card instance is simply discarded. The name promises more than the implementation delivers - a good review catch.

items.prompt: A create-card request carries an assigneeId that is a valid GUID but belongs to nobody on the board. What comes back?
items.answer: A 400 problem with code member.not_found, because the aggregate requires assignees to be board members
distractors: A 404, since the referenced member resource does not exist
A 201 - assignees are free-form GUIDs and membership is not checked
A 409 conflict flagging a stale member list on the client
items.explanation: EnsureAssigneeExists scans _members and throws DomainException.BadRequest("member.not_found", "Assignee is not a member of this board.") when no id matches; null assignees are allowed.

items.prompt: How does a DomainException thrown deep in the aggregate reach the HTTP client?
items.answer: Middleware catches it and writes application/problem+json with the exception's status, plus code and traceId stuffed into ProblemDetails.Extensions
distractors: Each endpoint wraps its service call in try/catch and maps codes to Results helpers
ASP.NET's built-in developer exception page serializes it as HTML in all environments
The service layer converts it to a Result<T> that endpoints pattern-match on
items.explanation: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware has catch arms for DomainException (its own StatusCode), BadHttpRequestException (400) and everything else (500, detail hidden outside Development); WriteProblemAsync adds the code and traceId extensions.

items.prompt: A mutation arrives with the header 'X-Board-Version: abc'. What is the outcome?
items.answer: 400 with code board.version_invalid, thrown before the service mutation ever runs
distractors: The header is ignored as if absent, and the mutation proceeds unchecked
409 board.version_conflict, since 'abc' can never equal the current version
500 server.unhandled, because int.Parse throws an uncaught FormatException
items.explanation: ReadExpectedVersion distinguishes absent (null, check skipped) from present-but-unparsable, which throws DomainException.BadRequest("board.version_invalid", ...) via int.TryParse.

items.prompt: Why can code that fetched a Board via GetAsync freely call mutators on it without corrupting the stored state?
items.answer: The repository returns a deep Clone - stored boards never escape, so callers always hold a detached copy
distractors: Board instances are immutable records, so mutators return new objects anyway
GetAsync takes the write lock, so the caller holds exclusive access while mutating
It cannot - mutating a fetched board silently mutates the shared store
items.explanation: GetAsync returns `stored.Clone()` (and UpdateAsync both mutates a clone and stores a clone). Board.Clone deep-copies columns and cards, giving clone-in/clone-out isolation.

items.prompt: What must a caller prove before PATCHing a card on someone's board in this codebase?
items.answer: Nothing - no endpoint requires authorization or checks identity; board members exist purely as display data
distractors: Membership of the board, enforced by the EnsureAssigneeExists guard on every mutation
A valid session cookie issued by the client app's login flow
Possession of the board's version token, which acts as a capability secret
items.explanation: The guide's auth-boundary section: no RequireAuthorization, no [Authorize], no identity checks; members live in seed storage as display data, not security principals. The assignee guard validates data, not callers.

items.front: NetTrello's Guard.Required does more than validate. What exactly does the stored value look like?
items.back: The value is trimmed first; whitespace-only input throws validation.required, over-length trimmed input throws validation.max_length, and the TRIMMED string is what the domain keeps - normalization and validation in one step.

items.front: A board fresh out of POST /api/boards already reports Version 5. Walk through why.
items.back: The constructor starts Version at 1, then CreateBoardAsync adds the four default columns (Backlog, In progress, Review, Done) and every AddColumn calls Touch, which increments Version - 1 + 4 bumps = 5.

items.front: The critique ranks 'optional version header' as risk 4. What is the failure mode and the recommended fix?
items.back: Because ReadExpectedVersion returns null when X-Board-Version is absent, any client can bypass optimistic-concurrency conflict checks and overwrite newer state; the recommendation is to require the header on all mutations.
